description: The State Legislature is the supreme law-making body at the state level. Panchayati Raj is a system of rural local self-government in India, primarily aimed at promoting democracy and development at the grassroots level.

sections.title: State Legislature: Structure and Functions
sections.description: Part VI of the Constitution describes the constitution, structure, and powers of the State Legislature.

key_concepts.explanation: Most states have only a Legislative Assembly, known as a unicameral legislature. States with both a Legislative Assembly and a Legislative Council are known as bicameral legislatures.

polity_articles.details: For every State there shall be a Legislature which shall consist of the Governor and one or two Houses.

polity_articles.provision: Abolition or Creation of Legislative Councils
polity_articles.details: Parliament may by law provide for the abolition or creation of a Legislative Council if the Legislative Assembly of the State passes a resolution to that effect by a special majority.
The maximum number of members in a Legislative Assembly can be 500 and the minimum 60, with a few special exceptions.

important_facts.fact: Currently, only 6 states in India have a Bicameral Legislature: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.

sections.title: Historical Evolution of Panchayati Raj
sections.description: Various committees were formed and historical steps were taken to provide constitutional status to local self-government in India.

historical_events.significance: The country's first three-tier Panchayat was inaugurated by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in Nagaur district of Rajasthan.
This landmark act granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).

key_associations.extra_info: Recommended the establishment of Panchayats at the Village, Block, and District levels.
Suggested the replacement of the three-tier system with a two-tier system consisting of Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat.
This committee first advocated for constitutional recognition and regular free and fair elections for Panchayats.

sections.title: 73rd Amendment and Important Articles
sections.description: The 73rd Amendment of 1992 added Part IX and the 11th Schedule to the Indian Constitution.

polity_articles.details: A body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of the Panchayat at the village level.
Mandates the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in proportion to their population and at least one-third (1/3rd) of total seats for women.
Constituted by the Governor every five years to review the financial position of the Panchayats and recommend fund distribution.
Responsible for the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all Panchayat elections.

important_facts.fact: The 11th Schedule of the Constitution contains 29 functional items placed within the purview of Panchayati Raj Institutions.

sections.title: Government Schemes Related to Panchayati Raj
sections.description: Major schemes launched by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj for rural development and the empowerment of PRIs.

key_associations.extra_info: Aims to provide an integrated property validation solution for rural India by demarcating inhabited land using drone technology.
A scheme designed to empower Panchayati Raj Institutions to achieve Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
A unified digital platform for comprehensive planning, accounting, and monitoring of Panchayat development activities.

important_facts.fact: National Panchayati Raj Day is celebrated across India every year on 24 April to mark the enactment of the 73rd Amendment Act in 1993.
